title: Definitions - Licensee, Licensor, Standard Rent, Tenant
content: Defines Licensee as a person given a license for occupation of premises; Licensor as the person giving license; Tenant as any person by whom or on whose account rent is payable; and Standard Rent as rent fixed by the Court or specified under the Act.
key_legal_takeaway: Establishes legal status distinguishing a tenant (with tenancy rights) from a licensee (with limited occupational license).

title: Rent in excess of standard rent illegal
content: Save as otherwise provided in Section 11, it shall not be lawful to claim, demand or receive any increase in rent, or any sum as premium or fine for the grant, renewal or continuance of a tenancy.
key_legal_takeaway: Landlords cannot demand arbitrary or illegal rent increases beyond statutory limits.

title: Increase in rent annually and for improvements
content: A landlord shall be entitled to make an annual increase in rent of not more than 4 per cent per annum in respect of premises let for residential purpose, and up to 15 per cent per annum where improvements or structural alterations are executed.
key_legal_takeaway: Caps annual rent escalation at 4% per annum unless structural improvements are made by the landlord.

title: Prohibition of claiming premium or excessive security deposit
content: It shall not be lawful for any landlord or person acting on behalf of landlord to claim or receive any premium, pugree or other like sum or any consideration as a condition of grant, renewal or continuance of tenancy.
key_legal_takeaway: Prohibits extortionate premiums (Pugree) and excessive non-refundable deposit demands.

title: No ejectment ordinarily to be made if tenant pays standard rent
content: A landlord shall not be entitled to the recovery of possession of any premises so long as the tenant pays, or is ready and willing to pay, the amount of the standard rent and permitted increases, if any, and observes and performs the other conditions of the tenancy.
key_legal_takeaway: Protecting tenants against arbitrary eviction as long as rent payments and essential contractual covenants are satisfied.

title: When landlord may recover possession (Eviction Grounds)
content: A landlord may recover possession of premises if tenant has committed breach of contract, created nuisance or annoyance, sublet the premises without written consent, or if landlord requires premises for bona fide personal occupation.
key_legal_takeaway: Eviction is permissible only under strict statutory grounds such as non-payment, unauthorized subletting, or genuine personal necessity.

title: Landlord entitled to recover possession of premises given on license on expiry
content: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, a licensee in possession or occupation of premises delivered to him on license for residential use shall deliver possession of such premises to the landlord on expiry of the period of license; and, on the failure of the licensee to so deliver the possession of the licensed premises, a landlord shall be entitled to recover possession of such premises by making an application to the Competent Authority. Any licensee who fails to deliver possession on expiry of license period shall be liable to pay damages at double the rate of license fee.
key_legal_takeaway: Under Maharashtra Rent Control Act Section 24, a licensee must hand over possession upon expiry of license. Unlawful holdover attracts damages up to double the monthly license fee.

title: Landlord not to cut off or withhold essential supply or service
content: No landlord either himself or through any person acting or purporting to act on his behalf shall without just or sufficient cause cut off or withhold any essential supply or service enjoyed by the tenant in respect of the premises let to him. Essential supply includes water, electricity, lights in passages and staircases, and sanitary services.
key_legal_takeaway: Landlords are strictly prohibited from cutting off electricity, water, or basic amenities as a coercion tactic.

title: Tenancy agreement to be in writing and registered
content: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or any other law for the time being in force, any agreement for leave and license or letting of any premises shall be in writing and shall be registered under the Registration Act, 1908. The responsibility of getting such agreement registered shall be upon the landlord. In the absence of a written registered agreement, the contention of the tenant about the terms and conditions shall prevail.
key_legal_takeaway: Registration of Leave & License agreements is compulsory in Maharashtra. Responsibility lies on the landlord; failure means tenant/licensee terms prevail.

title: Lease defined, Lessor, Lessee, Premium and Rent defined
content: A lease of immovable property is a transfer of a right to enjoy such property, made for a certain time, express or implied, or in perpetuity, in consideration of a price paid or promised, or of money, a share of crops, service or any other thing of value.
key_legal_takeaway: Defines the core legal interest transferred under a lease agreement.

title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
content: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for agricultural or manufacturing purposes shall be deemed to be a lease from year to year, terminable by six months notice; and a lease for any other purpose shall be deemed to be a lease from month to month, terminable by fifteen days notice.
key_legal_takeaway: Establishes default statutory notice periods of 15 days for monthly residential/commercial leases.

title: Rights and liabilities of Lessor and Lessee
content: The lessor is bound to disclose any material defect in the property and bound to bind himself to the covenant of quiet enjoyment. The lessee is bound to pay rent at the appointed time, maintain the property in good condition, and restore the property without unreasonable damage. The lessee may sub-let or transfer his interest unless expressly restricted by the lease contract.
key_legal_takeaway: Establishes mutual statutory obligations: lessor guarantees peaceful enjoyment; lessee is responsible for reasonable maintenance and timely payments.

title: Determination of lease
content: A lease of immovable property determines by efflux of time, by the happening of an event, by surrender, or by notice to quit or of intention to determine the lease. In case of forfeiture for breach of express condition, reasonable notice of breach must be provided before enforcement.
key_legal_takeaway: Termination of lease requires due compliance with notice terms or efflux of time; forfeiture requires clear notice of breach.

title: What agreements are contracts - Free consent & lawful consideration
content: All agreements are contracts if they are made by the free consent of parties competent to contract, for a lawful consideration and with a lawful object, and are not hereby expressly declared to be void.
key_legal_takeaway: Every contract clause requires free consent, lawful object, and capacity to be enforceable.

title: What consideration and objects are lawful, and what not
content: The consideration or object of an agreement is lawful, unless it is forbidden by law, or is of such a nature that, if permitted, it would defeat the provisions of any law, or is fraudulent, or involves or implies injury to the person or property of another, or the Court regards it as immoral, or opposed to public policy.
key_legal_takeaway: Clauses that defeat statutory rights or violate public policy are void ab initio.

title: Agreement in restraint of trade void
content: Every agreement by which any one is restrained from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business of any kind, is to that extent void.
key_legal_takeaway: Unreasonable non-competes and trade restrictions are void under Indian law.

title: Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings void
content: Every agreement by which any party thereto is restricted absolutely from enforcing his rights under or in respect of any contract, by the usual legal proceedings in the ordinary tribunals, or which limits the time within which he may thus enforce his rights, is void to that extent.
key_legal_takeaway: Clauses that completely prohibit a tenant or landlord from seeking legal recourse or court remedies are legally void.

title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
content: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby, which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, to be likely to result from the breach of it.
key_legal_takeaway: Damages are restricted to actual, direct losses naturally arising from a breach.

title: Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for
content: When a contract has been broken, if a sum is named in the contract as the amount to be paid in case of such breach, or if the contract contains any other stipulation by way of penalty, the party complaining of the breach is entitled, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved to have been caused thereby, to receive from the party who has broken the contract reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or the penalty stipulated for.
key_legal_takeaway: Excessive or oppressive daily penalties and total security deposit forfeitures are unenforceable. Courts and arbitrators award only reasonable compensation for actual loss under Section 74.
